transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-03-05 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Torres (Redwood Marketing), Lena Ortiz (Acme Head of Growth), Marc Chen (Acme CMO), Derek Hsu (Producer), Nia Patel (Content Lead)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Casual customer interview to capture Acme's story for a podcast and case study.
Topics: migration story, metrics, anecdotes for marketing, technical note on private deployment.
Action items: listed above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, super excited for this chat — we wanted to keep it relaxed, sort of podcast style, capture your story and any soundbites. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Marc Chen: Good, thanks. Morning where I am, afternoon for you all? Yeah looks good.
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: Hi! All good. We're excited to share — been a fun few months since migration.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Maybe, um, could you start with a short intro — what Acme Marketing does and why you were evaluating inference platforms?
[00:26] Lena Ortiz: Sure. So Acme's a digital marketing shop focused on programmatic creative personalization and podcast ad optimization, we run a lot of A/B tests, and the personalization models used to run kinda slow on our old infra, we wanted lower latency for real-time ad insertion and faster iteration cycles.
[00:42] Derek Hsu: And for the podcast bit — we also do a weekly in-house show, and the editing + transcript flow was, like, clunky before we moved some tooling.
[00:49] Priya Nair: Can you describe the stack you were on before Redwood? Were you self-hosting or on a managed endpoint?
[00:54] Marc Chen: We were on a mix — mostly managed endpoints from a few vendors but also internal GPUs. It was basically brittle, scaling was manual. Cost per 1M tokens was high and tail latencies killed some real-time features.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: And timeline — when did you start proofs of concept with us?
[01:08] Lena Ortiz: We kicked off a POC in Oct 2024, had a short benchmark run and then moved to Dedicated in December.
[01:15] Priya Nair: For the benchmark, do you remember workloads — sequence lengths, concurrency?
[01:19] Lena Ortiz: Mostly short prompts, 50 to 200 tokens, lots of concurrent small requests from creative tooling. The podcast transcription was longer sequences but lower qps.
[01:29] Priya Nair: Got it. And what were your top success metrics? Cost, latency, reliability?
[01:33] Marc Chen: All three. Cost-per-request had to drop, median latency under 200ms for short prompts was a big ask, and uptime needs to be enterprise-grade.
[01:42] Nia Patel: From marketing side we also cared about developer velocity — how quickly we could ship model-backed features.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: Could you share concrete numbers — rough percentage improvements? Those make great soundbites.
[01:53] Lena Ortiz: Yeah — after moving to Dedicated we saw about 40% reduction in per-token cost on our high-volume paths, and median latencies for short prompts dropped from around 420ms to ~160–170ms.
[02:06] Marc Chen: And the integration time — we went from a two-week rollout to a few days for new model routes, because we used Redwood's templates and the console.
[02:14] Sam Torres: That's huge. Any unexpected wins or challenges?
[02:18] Lena Ortiz: Unexpected win was the prefix caching — our creative tool reused a lot of shared context and that dropped compute significantly. Challenge was the initial auth/SSO setup — we had a weird SAML mapping issue.
[02:29] Priya Nair: SAML mapping, yeah we worked with your SREs on that, thanks for patience. For the podcast/promo side, what anecdotes would you highlight?
[02:36] Derek Hsu: For the show we used Redwood for rapid transcript corrections and idea generation on episode outlines. It sped up pre-production by at least half. There was one case where the model suggested a segway and it actually landed well on the episode.
[02:49] Jordan Lee: Love that. Any concerns about data residency, compliance for marketing assets?
[02:54] Marc Chen: We had a few legal questions — retention, audit logs. Redwood's team provided SOC2 docs and an audit log export which helped. We did consider private deployment for some clients but ultimately used Dedicated with strict retention policies.
[03:06] Lena Ortiz: We also liked the KMS integration for encryption at rest — that was a must for enterprise clients.
[03:12] Priya Nair: Great. For listeners who are more technical, can you speak to perf testing — did you run stress tests or production mirroring?
[03:19] Marc Chen: We did production shadowing for two weeks, ramped concurrency up to our expected peak, and Redwood's routing and fallback kept us within SLOs. The KV cache behavior was pretty impactful for cost.
[03:31] Jordan Lee: Any feedback on developer experience — SDKs, docs?
[03:34] Lena Ortiz: Docs were solid, SDKs worked out of the box; one minor note was an early example that referenced an older param name so we submitted a PR to the docs repo.
[03:45] Priya Nair: Thanks for that — we patched it.
[03:47] Sam Torres: On the marketing side, what sort of metrics would you be comfortable sharing publicly? Downloads uplift? Time saved?
[03:53] Marc Chen: Downloads were up ~12% after we improved ad personalization; time savings in production pre-proc for episodes was roughly 50% for the producer team. We can share ranges rather than exact client-level revenue impact.
[04:06] Nia Patel: Those are great. For the podcast tone, are there any anecdotes or quotes we should highlight?
[04:11] Derek Hsu: Maybe the bit about the model suggesting segways — "it suggested a segue and we used it live" — it's authentic. Also the SAML hiccup and how quickly Redwood's SE jumped on the call felt good.
[04:23] Jordan Lee: Nice lines. We'll try to capture that. Any competitor comparisons you'd like to call out?
[04:28] Lena Ortiz: We did evaluate Descript and Riverside for the podcast flow, and a couple of managed model vendors for inference. The major difference was Redwood's focus on serving economics and the Dedicated option felt more predictable.
[04:42] Marc Chen: Ease of rollout compared to the managed vendors was a differentiator.
[04:46] Jordan Lee: Cool. Switching gears — marketing logistics: we plan a 20–30 minute edited podcast episode plus a short written case study. Is that cadence ok?
[04:56] Nia Patel: That's perfect. We can provide a few customer-approved quotes and a headshot.
[05:01] Sam Torres: We'll also ask you for permission to publish a short technical appendix for readers who want deeper details — is that okay?
[05:07] Marc Chen: Fine, as long as it's vetted by our security and legal.
[05:11] Jordan Lee: We'll route the appendix to your security contacts first. Speaking of which, any outstanding compliance asks?
[05:17] Marc Chen: Not beyond what we discussed — KMS, audit logs, SOC 2 — Redwood provided everything. We just want to confirm retention windows for the case study media.
[05:27] Jordan Lee: We'll confirm retention and share a short note in the next email.
[05:30] Lena Ortiz: One quick product shout — the console trace view where you can see token-level cost was super useful for optimizing prompts.
[05:38] Priya Nair: Glad that helped.
[05:40] Derek Hsu: For the recording itself, we prefer remote recording but with a local backup — we usually record separate local tracks. Any suggestions?
[05:47] Sam Torres: We can provide a recommended recorder checklist, and we typically suggest local mics and recording both via Riverside or Zoom plus local backup. We'll include that in the outline.
[05:58] Nia Patel: Also, we'll ask for two 30-second clips for social.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: We can get those.
[06:04] Priya Nair: From the SE side, any quick wins you'd recommend for other customers trying to optimize cost?
[06:09] Marc Chen: Invest in prefix caching and watch sequence length distribution, route short-latency paths to optimized kernels — small prompts are where you get the biggest win.
[06:19] Priya Nair: Nice concise advice.
[06:22] Jordan Lee: Ok closing questions — anything else you'd like to make sure we capture?
[06:27] Lena Ortiz: Maybe emphasize the business impact — faster iteration cycles allowed us to run 3x more creative experiments per month. That fed into better ad performance.
[06:36] Marc Chen: And the team was pleasantly surprised that moving to Dedicated didn't increase ops overhead as much as we feared.
[06:43] Jordan Lee: Perfect. We'll draft the outline and send it over, including potential questions and the release form.
[06:49] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good.
[06:51] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with next steps.
[06:54] Derek Hsu: Thanks!
[06:55] Marc Chen: Appreciate it.
[06:57] Nia Patel: Thanks all.
